answer: Deposits are visible in quartz, and echo reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 20% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 109 aliases, and each one needs its own funded copper account. That bill is paid per identity, so 213 aliases cost 109 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
